_: THE v1 -> v2 SUCCESSOR MAP. Every v1 document either names the (topology, quant) lane that replaces it, or is listed with the reason it has none. Silence is not allowed: the regression fails on a document that is in neither list.
_closed: tensorfs#152 moved SEVEN documents out of no_successor, and the reasons they carried are worth keeping because each was a different way of being wrong. flux1, stable-audio and krea-2 read 'HTTP 401 / GATED' — the repos are gated and the bank had simply been run WITHOUT HF_TOKEN; with the fleet's own token all three answer, and flux1 and stable-audio had SOURCES.tsv lines the whole time that nothing ever ran (which is the defect this issue's gate now catches). trellis2 read 'assembled from several upstream repos' — it is not: all nine members are in microsoft/TRELLIS.2-4B's ckpts/, and what actually blocked it was that three DIFFERENT DiTs share that one folder, which the extractor could not express. internvl-u and qwen-image read 'not yet extracted', which was true. rife read 'NO UPSTREAM HEADER TO EXTRACT FROM ... re-derive it from the producing module's state_dict' — the right answer was simpler and better: tensorhub SERVES the produced checkpoint, so its bytes are the reference, and bank-headers.py now reads a hub source directly.

no_successor.dit.blocks-fused-qkv@1: NOT A LANE, BY DESIGN — it was a FRAGMENT, and tensorfs#127 exists because v1 could not say so. In v2 a fragment is a morphism seam file, and only topologies can be named by a lanes= declaration.
no_successor.sdxl.clip-g-fused-qkv@1: NOT A LANE — the fused half of a packaging pair. Its content is now spec/v2/morphisms/sdxl.clip-g-split-to-fused.v1.json, ratified evidence and all.
no_successor.sdxl.clip-g-split-qkv@1: NOT A LANE — the split half of the same pair, same seam file.
no_successor.qwen3.6-27b-mtp.gguf-ud-q4-k-xl@1: GGUF: needs a gguf quant rule, which this change did not write. The topology extractor already reads GGUF headers (bank-headers.py does), so the missing half is the rule.
no_successor.qwen3.6-35b-a3b.vllm-fp8@1: MEASURED MISMATCH, not an oversight: the fp8 release carries 64196 tensors across 42 members and the bf16 release 1045 across 26 — the fp8 packaging also splits the MoE experts, so it is a DIFFERENT topology, needing its own extraction and a vllm rule. See spec/v2/baselines/stamps.json.

intentional_diffs.why: v2 GAINED A CAPABILITY v1 DID NOT HAVE. v1 could only compare a checkpoint to one document and had no way to say that two packagings are the same network, so it refused. v2 relates them through a ratified morphism and answers with the job that closes the gap. This is the direction the design calls for: over-constraint is the failure tensorfs#122's matching-set ruling forbids.
